Topics · The holy books together

Why does the Quran appeal to Jewish scholars?

A new claim usually avoids old experts. The Quran names them as witnesses and says some believed. Weigh that.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَإِنَّهُۥ لَفِى زُبُرِ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ١٩٦ أَوَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ ءَايَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُۥ عُلَمَـٰٓؤُا۟ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ١٩٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

And indeed, it is [mentioned] in the scriptures of former peoples. And has it not been a sign to them that it is recognized by the scholars of the Children of Israel?

Quran · Ash-Shu'ara 26:196-197

Think how a new claim usually treats the experts of an older one: it avoids them. These verses do the opposite. It is in the writings of the ancients, they say. And they ask: was it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel knew it? The book names as its witnesses the people best placed to examine it. They were not its followers, and nothing bound them to help it. Only one willing to be examined makes such an appeal.

A question for you

What does someone risk by naming such people as witnesses?

If you sayBeing contradicted by them.
ThenThat is the risk. The third part says, honestly, what happened.
If you sayNothing, they were far away.
ThenNot all of them were far away: Yathrib had Jewish communities. That makes the risk plainer.
If you sayBeing told he learned from them.
ThenA sharp reply: a witness might be a source. It has its own Step, with the Quran's answer.

Part 2 of 3

﴿فَإِن كُنتَ فِى شَكٍّ مِّمَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ فَسْـَٔلِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقْرَءُونَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ مِن قَبْلِكَ ۚ لَقَدْ جَآءَكَ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

So if you are in doubt, [O Muḥammad], about that which We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so never be among the doubters.

Quran · Yunus 10:94

This verse goes further, and it is addressed to the Prophet himself: if you are in doubt about what We sent down to you, ask those who read the Book before you. The form is conditional. It does not say he doubted, and many commentators read it as speaking to every hearer. What it shows is a stance toward evidence: this truth does not dread the older book. It tells its own bearer: go and ask.

A question for you

What do you read in this sentence?

If you sayConfidence in the evidence.
ThenThat is close to the tone of the verse: go and ask.
If you sayThat he actually asked them.
ThenThe verse does not say so, though a historian may read it that way. See how the Quran answers on a teacher.
If you sayI am not sure.
ThenThat is fine. The next part asks whether anyone answered.

Part 3 of 3

﴿قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِن كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَكَفَرْتُم بِهِۦ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنۢ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ عَلَىٰ مِثْلِهِۦ فَـَٔامَنَ وَٱسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "Have you considered: if it [i.e., the Qur’ān] was from Allāh, and you disbelieved in it while a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar[1480] and believed while you were arrogant...?"[1481] Indeed, Allāh does not guide the wrongdoing people.

Translator's notes

[1480] Based upon information from the Torah. [1481] The conclusion is estimated to be "...would you not then be the most unjust of people?" or "...in what condition would you then be?"

Quran · Al-Ahqaf 46:10

﴿ٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيْنَـٰهُمُ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ هُم بِهِۦ يُؤْمِنُونَ٥٢ وَإِذَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مُسْلِمِينَ٥٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they[1111] are believers in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were, [even] before it, Muslims [i.e., submitting to Allāh]."

Translator's notes

[1111] i.e., the sincere believers among them.

Quran · Al-Qasas 28:52-53

Did anyone answer? The Quran says some did. A witness from the Children of Israel testified to the like of it and believed. Those given the Book before it say, when it is recited to them: we believe, it is the truth from our Lord, we had surrendered before it. The Quran says some, and not all. It does not claim the scholars of Israel as a body, then or since. Its claim is narrower and can stand: among those who knew the older books, some heard the same voice.

A question for you

Whose witness would weigh most with you?

If you sayA scholar of my own tradition.
ThenThen the Step on what is foretold sets out what the Quran says of your books.
If you sayMy own reading of the texts.
ThenThe best witness of all, and the texts are gathered in one Step.
If you saySomeone with nothing to gain.
ThenA good measure, and it can be applied to the Prophet himself.

Your reflection

Who is the person you wish you could ask about all of this, and why that one?
